summary: The exact 103-file candidate byte set remains unchanged, unique, allowlisted, excludes Session B artifacts, and recomputes to the expected file-set SHA256. Reviewer profile, assignment, run and session bindings also match, and all filed production suites report PASS. Formal Security approval is nevertheless blocked by two evidence-integrity defects: the filed Session B security-evidence artifact declares scan_contract_version 4 while the bound production scan contract is version 5, and the formal read scope omits the governance manifest, bootstrap candidate record and bootstrap scanner report whose direct independent verification was required. No Human Commit GO or Migration 320 approval is declared.

binding_assessment.scope_hash_canonicalization: SHA256 of canonical compact JSON containing allowed_files, forbidden_roots, assignment_id, reviewer_run_id and session_id.

candidate_integrity.direct_read_absence_reason: These three referenced source artifacts are not entries in the formal allowed_files list.

findings.subject: .codex/tasks/GOV-PHASE1-SESSION-B-COMPATIBILITY-REVIEW/security-evidence.yaml
findings.description: The filed Session B security evidence declares scan_contract_version 4, but the exact allowlisted production scan-contract artifact declares scan_contract_version 5 and hashes to 6A0EF0CAEE9088D65616DA318DB895321DF4D932C7308E2522D35F8242F4816C.
findings.impact: The formal evidence misidentifies the contract purportedly executed. The zero-finding claim cannot be accepted as an internally consistent Session B security assertion until the version and hash binding are corrected and independently reviewed.

findings.subject: .codex/tasks/GOV-PHASE1-SESSION-B-COMPATIBILITY-REVIEW/security-review-read-scope.json
findings.description: The formal allowed_files list excludes .codex/governance/governance-commit-manifest.yaml, .codex/tasks/GOV-PHASE1-REMEDIATION-9/bootstrap-candidate-record.json and .codex/tasks/GOV-PHASE1-REMEDIATION-9/bootstrap-scanner-report.json.
findings.impact: The reviewer cannot directly hash or validate the three source artifacts required for independent manifest, candidate-record and scanner-report chain verification. Filed summaries and frozen baselines agree, but they do not replace direct source-byte verification.

conditions.required_action: Correct the Session B security-evidence scan_contract_version to 5, bind the exact scan-contract SHA256, regenerate applicable evidence, and validate it without altering the reviewed 103-file candidate.

Create a fresh formal Security review scope that explicitly allowlists the governance commit manifest, bootstrap candidate record and bootstrap scanner report, then perform a new clean, read-only independent verification of their bytes, payload hashes, schemas and cross-bindings.
Keep Human Commit GO, steady-state activation and Migration 320 execution blocked while these findings remain open.

residual_risks: SHA256 establishes byte integrity and equality only; it does not establish trusted producer identity, source truth, Git authority or human authorization.
The deterministic scanner covers only declared registered classes and the exact candidate set. It is explicitly not DLP and does not prove global sensitive-data absence.
Compressed, encrypted, fragmented, unknown or beyond-contract multiply encoded content may evade the scanner.
Reviewer identity and clean-context separation are procedural, not cryptographic person identity or OS-enforced isolation.
The agent path policy is a commit-time role-scope gate with runtime_isolation=false; it is not an operating-system sandbox.
The production suite results were verified from filed reports and were not rerun by this reviewer.
The governance manifest, candidate record and scanner report were not directly readable within this formal scope.
